title: Intelligent Robot Path Planning Performance Optimization and Control Strategy Integrating Reinforcement Learning and AlphaEvolve
venue: 2nd International Conference on Electronic Circuits and Signaling Technologies (ICECST)

publication.venue: 2nd International Conference on Electronic Circuits and Signaling Technologies (ICECST)

mechanism.domainTask: Robot path planning with BEV perception, PPO/LLM-DQN control, and AlphaEvolve optimization
mechanism.populationDetail: The paper says AlphaEvolve performs global optimization but does not specify what candidate set or population structure it maintains.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No archive design is described; the named AlphaEvolve module alone is insufficient evidence to infer one.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The paper does not expose evolutionary candidate storage, admission or removal rules.
mechanism.generationDetail: AlphaEvolve is said to optimize policy parameters and path-node selection, but the parent-offspring relation and candidate-generation procedure are not described.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: The stated AlphaEvolve objective combines weighted path cost with energy/action cost; reported simulation metrics include path length, smoothness, energy use, planning time and success rate. Their use as additional feedback in evolution is not described.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: No evolutionary parent-selection procedure is described.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: A hybrid robotics control architecture combines BEV visual perception, PPO/LLM-DQN, AlphaEvolve policy/path optimization, and heuristic A*/artificial-potential-field adjustments; the evolutionary internals are not exposed.
